commands.name: GOTO
commands.description: Don't use this command.  It jumps directly to a label defined by @#SUBR@. This command is only here because it is used implicitly by @#DOIF@ blocks. This is a really dangerous command to use manually, because if you jump out of a block of code (eg a @#LOOP@...@#EVER@ block), the stack frame will no longer be correct, and the script will most likely crash. Don't use it!  See @#SUBR@.

commands.name: STOP
commands.description: Stops running the current script.  Compare @#STPT@.

commands.name: GSUB
commands.description: Jumps to a subroutine defined by @#SUBR@. Execution will continue at the instruction after the GSUB when the subroutine hits a @#RETN@ command.

commands.name: CALL

parameters.name: script_no
parameters.description: Event/script number to run on OWNR

parameters.name: p1
parameters.description: First parameter, available to the called script as _P1_

parameters.name: p2
parameters.description: Second parameter, available to the called script as _P2_

commands.description: Calls script_no on OWNR, then waits for it to return.  The invoked script inherits the caller's INST setting, but any changes it makes to INST are reversed once it returns.  Script variables (VAxx) are NOT preserved across the call - use OVxx for parameters.  In this rebuild CALL is executed natively by the bytecode VM via a per-agent call-frame stack (the interpreter fallback path does not support CALL).  See also @#GSUB@.

commands.name: RETN
commands.description: Return from subroutine. Do not use this instruction from inside a block of code (eg a @#LOOP@#..@#EVER@ or @#ENUM@...@#NEXT@ etc...)!  See @#SUBR@ and @#GSUB@.

commands.name: TARG
commands.description: This sets the TARG variable to the agent specified.

commands.name: KILL
commands.description: Destroys an agent.  The pointer won't be destroyed.  For creatures, you probably want to use @#DEAD@ first.

commands.name: TICK
commands.description: Start agent timer, calling @#Timer@ script every tick_rate ticks.  Set to 0 to turn off the timer.

commands.name: ADDV
commands.description: Adds two integers or floats, so var = var + sum.

commands.name: SUBV
commands.description: Subtracts an integer or float from a variable, so var = var - sub.

commands.name: MULV
commands.description: Multiplies a variable by an integer or float, so var = var * mul.

commands.name: DIVV
commands.description: Divides a variable by an integer or float, so var = var / div.  Uses integer division if both numbers are integers, or floating point division otherwise.

commands.name: MODV
commands.description: Gives the remainder (or modulus) when a variable is divided by an integer, so var = var % mod.  Both values should to be integers.

commands.name: NEGV
commands.description: Reverse the sign of the given integer or float variable, so var = 0 - var.

commands.name: ANDV
commands.description: Peform a bitwise AND on an integer variable, so var = var & value.

commands.name: ORRV
commands.description: Peform a bitwise OR on an integer variable, so var = var | value.

commands.name: SETV
commands.description: Stores an integer or float in a variable.

commands.name: STAR
commands.description: Randomly chooses an agent which matches the given classifier and can be seen by the owner of the script. It then sets @#TARG@ to that agent.  See @#ESEE@ for an explanation of seeing.
commands.example:
STAR 1 0 0  // Find any Norn
STAR 2 1 3  // Find specific Grendel type

commands.name: RTAR
commands.description: Randomly chooses an agent which matches the given classifier, and targets it.
commands.example:
RTAR 1 0 0  // Find any Norn
RTAR 2 1 3  // Find specific Grendel type

commands.name: INST
commands.description: This command indicates that the following commands should execute in a single tick - ie the script cannot be interrupted by the script 'scheduler'. This can be important for certain tasks which might leave an agent in an undefined (and dangerous) state if interrupted. The INST state is broken either manually, using a @#SLOW@ command, or implictly, if a blocking instruction is encountered (eg @#WAIT@). Blocking instructions force the remainder of the script's timeslice to be discarded.

commands.name: SLOW
commands.description: Turn off @#INST@ state.

commands.name: TTAR
commands.description: Randomly chooses an agent which matches the given classifier and is touching the owner of the script. It then sets @#TARG@ to that agent.  See @#ETCH@.
commands.example:
TTAR 1 0 0  // Find any Norn
TTAR 2 1 3  // Find specific Grendel type

commands.name: WAIT
commands.description: Block the script for the specified number of ticks. This command does an implicit @#SLOW@.

commands.name: ANIM
commands.description: Specify a list of @#POSE@s such as [1 2 3] to animate the current agent/part.  Put 255 at the end to continually loop.  The first number after the 255 is an index into the animation string where the looping restarts from - this defaults to 0 if not specified.  e.g. [0 1 2 10 11 12 255 3] would loop just the 10, 11, 12 section.

commands.name: OVER
commands.description: Wait until the current agent/part's @#ANIM@ation is over before continuing.  Looping anims stop this command terminating until the animation is changed to a non-looping one.

commands.name: POSE
commands.description: Specify a frame in the sprite file for the target agent/part.  Relative to any index specified by @#BASE@.

commands.name: GAIT
commands.description: Specifies the current gait for a creature. The gaits are genetically defined. It sets the gait of the creature agent stored in @#TARG@.

commands.name: BASE
commands.description: Set the base image for this agent or part.  The index is relative to the first_image specified in the NEW: command.  Future @#POSE@/@#ANIM@ commands and any @#ANIM@ in progress are relative to this new base.

commands.name: ABBA
commands.description: Returns the first_image (ie, absolute base) value for the TARG agent/part, or -1 if it has no image.  This is the absolute sprite index at which the agent's gallery begins, distinct from @#BASE@ (the relative animation base).

commands.name: DROP
commands.description: Causes the TARG agent to drop what it is carrying in a safe location.

commands.name: MVTO
commands.description: Move the top left corner of the target agent to the given world coordinates.  Use @#MVFT@ instead to move creatures.

commands.name: MVSF
commands.description: Move the target agent into a safe map location somewhere in the vicinity of x, y. Only works on autonomous agents - see @#MOVS@.  Works like a safe @#MVFT@ for creatures.

commands.name: MVBY
commands.description: Move the target agent by relative distances, which can be negative or positive.

commands.name: MVFT
commands.description: Move creature's down foot to position x,y.  Use this instead of @#MVTO@ for creatures.

commands.name: ABSV
commands.description: Set a variable to its absolute value, so if var is negative var = 0 - var, otherwise var is left alone.

commands.name: DELR
commands.description: Deletes the specified room from the map.

commands.name: DELM
commands.description: Deletes the specified metaroom from the map.

commands.name: PART
commands.description: Sets the working part number.  Future command such as @#POSE@ and @#ANIM@, amongst others, act on that part of a compound agent.

commands.name: CABN
commands.description: Set a vehicles cabin rectangle.  The cabin is the area in which agents inside the vehicle are kept.  The rectangle is relative to the position of the vehicle.  Default cabin is the bounding rectangle of part 0.  You might want to use @#ATTR@ to set attribute @#Greedy Cabin@, on the vehicle.  This will make it automatically pick up items which are dropped in the cabin.

commands.name: DPAS
commands.description: Drop all passengers matching classifier.

commands.name: GPAS
commands.description:
Collect all nearby agents matching the classifier as passengers.
rect_to_use 0 : Nearby means touching bounding rectangle of agent
rect_to_use 1 : Nearby means touching cabin rectangle

commands.name: SPAS
commands.description: Specified vehicle picks up the specified passenger.

commands.name: LOCI
commands.syntax: LOCI type organ tissue id new_value
commands.description: Sets a biochemical locus value.  See @#Receptor Locus Numbers@ and @#Emitter Locus Numbers@
commands.example: LOCI type organ tissue id new_value

commands.name: RMSC
commands.description: Associates a music track with the room at the specified coordinates.  This overrides any track specified for the metaroom that the room is in.

commands.name: RCLR
commands.description: Clear the music for the room at the given location.

commands.name: SNDE
commands.description: Play a sound effect audible as if emitted from target's current location.

commands.name: SNDQ
commands.description: As @#SNDE@, only with a delay before playing.

commands.name: SNDC
commands.description: Plays a controlled sound effect emitted from the target.  Updates volume and panning as the agent moves.

commands.name: SNDL
commands.description: Play a sound effect as in @#SNDC@, only the sound is looped.

commands.name: STPC
commands.description: Stops a controlled sound.

commands.name: FADE
commands.description: Fade out a controlled sound.

commands.name: CHEM
commands.description: Adjusts chemical (0 to 255) by concentration -1.0 to +1.0 in the target creature's bloodstream.

commands.name: INJR
commands.description: Injures an organ, -1 to randomly choose the organ, 0 for the body organ.

commands.name: APPR
commands.description: Creature approaches the IT agent.  If there is no IT agent, the creature follows the CA smell to find an agent of that category.  The script resumes when it gets there, or if it can't get any further.

commands.name: WALK
commands.description: Sets creature walking indefinitely. Chooses a walking gait according to chemo-receptors.  Always means ignore IT and walk in the current direction set by @#DIRN@.

commands.name: TOUC
commands.description: Make creature reach out to touch the IT agent.  Blocks the script until the creature either reaches the agent, or it's fully stretched and still can't.

commands.name: SAYN
commands.description: Creature expresses need, by speaking.

commands.name: LTCY
commands.description: Sets latency time on involuntary actions to a random value between min and max.  After an involuntary action occurs, the same action will not be able to kick in again until after that many ticks.  Min and max must range between 0 and 255.

commands.name: DREA
commands.description: Set to 1 to make the creature fall asleep and dream, 0 to stop the creature dreaming.  When dreaming, a creature's instincts are processed.  See also @#ASLP@.

commands.name: MATE
commands.description: Male creature mates with the IT agent - if IT is a female of the same genus!  The female doesn't need to be in reach.  If successful, the sperm is transmitted to the female and there is a chance of conception.  If pregnancy occurs, gene slot 1 of the mother contains the genome of the child.

commands.name: OUTS
commands.description: Sends a string to the output stream.  When running a script, the stream is null and this command does nothing.  For an externally injected command, the data from the stream is returned to the calling process.  For the @#CAOS@ command, the text is returned as a string.  You can use @#FILE OOPE@ to set the stream to a journal file.

commands.name: OUTX
commands.description:
This sends the string text to the output stream. However it first transforms any escapes into quoted escapes, and it also quotes the entire string for you.

e.g.:

outx \"Moooose\\n\"

Would produce:

\"Moooose\\n\"

on the output stream instead of:

Moooose

commands.name: OUTV
commands.description: Similar to @#OUTS@ only outputs a float or integer as a decimal string.

commands.name: DELG
commands.description: Deletes the specified @#GAME@ variable.

commands.name: DIRN
commands.description: Change creature to face a different direction. North 0, South 1, East 2, West 3.

commands.name: SCRX
commands.description: Remove specified script from the scriptorium.

commands.name: LOCK
commands.description: Prevent the current script being interrupted until @#UNLK@.  Normally, events other than timer scripts interrupt (abort) currently running scripts.  You can also use @#INST@ for similar, stronger protection.

commands.name: UNLK
commands.description: End the @#LOCK@ section.

commands.name: FRIC
commands.description: Set physics friction percentage, normally from 0 to 100.  Speed is lost by this amount when an agent slides along the floor.

commands.name: SETS
commands.description: Sets a variable to a string value.

commands.name: ADDS
commands.description: Concatenates two strings, so var = var + append.

commands.name: MAPK
commands.description: Resets the map to be empty.

commands.name: DOOR
commands.description: Sets the permiability of the door between two rooms.  This is used for both CAs and physical motion.  See also @#PERM@.

commands.name: MAPD
commands.description: Sets the dimensions of the map.  These are the maximum world coordinates.  Metarooms are rectangles within this area.

commands.name: ATTR
commands.description: Set attributes of target.  Sum the values in the @#Attribute Flags@ table to get the attribute value to pass into this command.

commands.name: IMSK
commands.description:
Set the input event mask. Indicates which types of global input events the agent is interested in, if any. For example, if the flag for \"key up\" events is set here, the agents \"key up\" script will be run every time a key is released.

Input event bit flags are
1 @#Raw Key Down@
2 @#Raw Key Up@
4 @#Raw Mouse Move@
8 @#Raw Mouse Down@
16 @#Raw Mouse Up@
32 @#Raw Mouse Wheel@
64 @#Raw Translated Char@

You can find the script numbers executed by following the links above.

commands.name: ACCG
commands.description: Set acceleration due to gravity in pixels per tick squared.

commands.name: SPIN

parameters.name: angle
parameters.description: Facing angle as a fraction of a full turn, wrapped into [0, 1).

commands.description: Docking Station: set or get (RV form) the angle (0.0 to 1.0) the target agent is facing. Only affects movement/display when the agent is rotatable (ATTR bit 1024).

commands.name: AVEL

parameters.name: angularvelocity
parameters.description: Angular velocity in turns per tick (added to SPIN each tick).

commands.description: Docking Station: set or get (RV form) the angular velocity of the target agent. Only affects movement when the agent is rotatable (ATTR bit 1024).

commands.name: FVEL

parameters.name: forwardvelocity
parameters.description: Forward velocity in pixels per tick along the facing direction.

commands.description: Docking Station: set or get (RV form) the forward velocity (in the rotated frame) of the target agent. Only affects movement when the agent is rotatable (ATTR bit 1024).

commands.name: SVEL

parameters.name: sidewaysvelocity
parameters.description: Sideways velocity in pixels per tick perpendicular to the facing direction.

commands.description: Docking Station: set or get (RV form) the sideways velocity (in the rotated frame) of the target agent. Only affects movement when the agent is rotatable (ATTR bit 1024).

commands.name: ADMP

parameters.name: angulardamping
parameters.description: Angular damping fraction per tick (0.0 to 1.0).

commands.description: Docking Station: set or get (RV form) the angular damping (0.0 to 1.0) of the target agent. Only affects movement when the agent is rotatable (ATTR bit 1024).

commands.name: FDMP

parameters.name: forwarddamping
parameters.description: Forward damping fraction per tick (0.0 to 1.0).

commands.description: Docking Station: set or get (RV form) the forward damping (0.0 to 1.0) of the target agent. Only affects movement when the agent is rotatable (ATTR bit 1024).

commands.name: SDMP

parameters.name: sidewaysdamping
parameters.description: Sideways damping fraction per tick (0.0 to 1.0).

commands.description: Docking Station: set or get (RV form) the sideways damping (0.0 to 1.0) of the target agent. Only affects movement when the agent is rotatable (ATTR bit 1024).

commands.name: ROTN

parameters.name: sprites
parameters.description: Number of sprites for each rotation frame (> 0).

parameters.name: rotations
parameters.description: Number of distinct rotation angles in the sprite file (> 0).

commands.description: Docking Station: enable automatic sprite adjustment for the target agent (changing the BASE of part 0) based on the current rotation (SPIN). Total sprites used = sprites * rotations. Only affects rotatable agents (ATTR bit 1024).

commands.name: ANGL
commands.description: Docking Station: returns the angle (0.0 to 1.0, north = 0 increasing clockwise) from the target agent's centre to the given coordinates. Works for any agent (does not require rotation).

commands.name: ELAS
commands.description: Set the elasticity percentage.  An agent with elasticity 100 will bounce perfectly, one with elasticity 0 won't bounce at all.

commands.name: AERO
commands.description: Set aerodynamic factor as a percentage.  The velocity is reduced by this factor each tick.

commands.name: CLAC
commands.description: Set the click action, which is the identifier of the message sent to the agent when it is clicked on, provided attribute @#Activateable@ is set.  Default is activate 1.  Use -1 to prevent it sending a message.  Also overriden by @#CLIK@.  Remember that the early @#Message Numbers@ differ slightly from @#Script Numbers@.

commands.name: SETA
commands.description: Stores a reference to an agent in a variable.

commands.name: ADDB
commands.description: Add a new background to the given metaroom.  Use @#BKGD@ to change the current displayed background.

commands.name: META
commands.description:
Change the current camera (set with @#SCAM@) to a new meta room. Moves the top left coordinate of the camera to the given coordinates.

Transition can be:
0 - no transition effect
1 - flip horizontally
2 - burst

commands.name: BKGD
commands.description: Change the current background displayed for the selected camera (with @#SCAM@).  Transition is as for @#META@.  The background must have been specified with the @#ADDM@ or @#ADDB@ command first.

commands.name: PERM
commands.description: Value from 1 to 100. Sets which room boundaries the agent can pass through.  The smaller the @#PERM@ the more it can go through.  @#DOOR@ sets the corresponding room boundary permiability.  Also used for @#ESEE@, to decide what it can see through.

commands.name: CMRA
commands.description: Move current camera so top left corner of view is at world coordinate x y. Set pan 0 to jump straight to location, pan 1 to smoothly scroll there (unless in a different meta room).

commands.name: CMRP
commands.description: Centre current camera on world coordinate x y. Set pan 0 to jump straight to location, pan 1 to smoothly scroll there (unless in different meta room), and pan 2 to smoothly scroll only if the destination is already visible.

commands.name: CMRT
commands.description: Centre current camera on target.  Set pan 0 to jump straight to location, pan 1 to smoothly scroll there (unless in different meta room), and pan 2 to smoothly scroll only if the destination is already visible.

commands.name: DMAP
commands.description: Set to 1 to turn the debug map image on, 0 to turn it off. The debug map includes vehicle cabin lines.

commands.name: RTYP
commands.description: Sets the type of a room.  The meaning of the types depends on the game.  @#RATE@ also uses the room type.

commands.name: PROP
commands.description: Sets the level of a CA (cellular automata) in a particular room.  There are 16 CAs, and their meaning depends on the game.  The level is between 0 and 1.

commands.name: RATE
commands.syntax: RATE room_type ca_index gain loss diffusion
commands.description: Sets various rates for a CA (cellular automata) in a particular type of room.  The values can be from 0 to 1.  Gain is the susceptibility to absorb from agents in the room, and loss is the amount lost to the atmosphere.  The diffusion is the amount it spreads to adjacent rooms.
commands.example: RATE room_type ca_index gain loss diffusion

commands.name: EMIT
commands.description: Target now constantly emits an amount of a CA into the room it is in.

commands.name: CACL
commands.description: This associates the classification specified with the CA specified. This allows the linking of CA's to classifiers within creatures' brains.

commands.name: ALTR
commands.description: Directly adjusts the level of a CA in a room.  Specify an identifier of -1 to use the room of the midpoint of the target agent.

commands.name: WEAR
commands.description: Sets a layer of clothing on part of the creature.  The set_number is the type of clothing to put on from the overlay file - think of it as an outfit number.  layer 0 is the actual body of the creature, so unless you want to replace the body part itself use a higher layer.  Higher layers are on top of lower ones. e.g. 0 for a face, 1 for measels spots, 2 for a fencing mask.  See also @#BODY@ and @#NUDE@.

commands.name: MIDI
commands.description: Plays a MIDI file.  Set to an empty string to stop the MIDI player.

commands.name: LINE
commands.syntax: LINE x1 y1 x2 y2 r g b stipple_on stipple_off
commands.description: Adds a line to target's drawing list.  The line goes between the start and end points (world coordinates) in the specified colour.  Set stipple_on and stipple_off to 0 to draw a solid line, or to the number of pixels to alternate for a stippled line.  To clear all the lines for an agent, call LINE with the start and end points the same.
commands.example: LINE x1 y1 x2 y2 r g b stipple_on stipple_off

commands.name: PLNE
commands.description: Sets the target agent's principal drawing plane.  The higher the value, the nearer the camera.  For compound agents, the principal plane is the one for the automatically made first part.  The plane of other parts is relative to this one.

commands.name: RNGE
commands.description: Sets the distance that the target can see and hear, and the distance used to test for potential collisions.  See also @#ESEE@, @#OBST@.

commands.name: CHAR
commands.description: Sets a character in a string.  String indices begin at 1.

commands.name: VELO
commands.description: Set velocity, measured in pixels per tick.

commands.name: RPAS
commands.description: Specified vehicle drops the specified passenger.

commands.name: PUPT
commands.description: Set the relative x and y coordinate of the place where target picks agents up, for the given pose.  This pose is measured from the absolute base specified in the NEW: command, rather than the relative base specified by the @#BASE@ command. Pose -1 sets the same point for all poses.  For vehicles use the @#CABN@ command.

commands.name: PUHL
commands.description: Set the relative x and y coordinate of the handle that target is picked up by, for the given pose.  This pose is measured from the absolute base specified in the NEW: command, rather than the relative base specified by the @#BASE@ command. Pose -1 sets the same point for all poses.

commands.name: CABP
commands.description: Set the plane that vehicle passengers are at.  This is relative to the vehicle's plane.

commands.name: TRCK
commands.syntax: TRCK agent x% y% style transition
commands.description:
Camera follows the given agent. Set to @#NULL@ to stop tracking. x% and y% are percentages (0-100) of the screen size. They describe a rectangle centred on the screen which the target stays within.
Style 0 is brittle - if you move the camera so the target is out of the rectangle, then the tracking is broken.
Style 1 is flexible - you can move the camera away from the target. If you move it back, then tracking resumes.
Style 2 is hard - you can't move the camera so the target is out of the rectangle.
The transition is the sort of fade to use if the tracking causes a change in meta room. The values are the same as for the transition in the @#META@ command.
commands.example: TRCK agent x% y% style transition

commands.name: GALL
commands.description: Changes the gallery (sprite file) used by an agent.  This works for simple and compound agents (using the current @#PART@).  The current @#POSE@ is kept the same in both galleries.

commands.name: ASLP
commands.description: Make the creature asleep or awake.  1 for asleep, 0 for awake.

commands.name: UNCS
commands.description: Make the creature conscious or unconscious.  0 for conscious, 1 for unconscious.

commands.name: BODY
commands.description: Similar to @#WEAR@, only puts the given set of clothes on every body part.

commands.name: NUDE
commands.description: Removes all clothes from a creature.  Any changed layer 0 will revert to drawing the body part again.  See @#WEAR@.

commands.name: AGES
commands.description: Forces a creature to age the given number of times.  See also @#CAGE@.

commands.name: DRIV
commands.description: Adjusts the level of the given drive by the specified amount - can be positive or negative.

commands.name: BHVR
commands.description: Sets the creature permissions for target.  Sum the entries in the @#Creature Permissions@ table to get the value to use.

commands.name: FACE
commands.description: Sets a facial expression on target creature.

commands.name: MCLR
commands.description: Clear the music for the metaroom at the given location.

commands.name: MMSC
commands.description: Associates a music track with the meta room at the specified coordinates.

commands.name: PTXT
commands.description: Set string of current text part.  Use @#PAT: TEXT@ or @#PAT: FIXD@ to make a text part, and @#PART@ to set the current part.

commands.name: NORN
commands.description: Chooses the active creature.  Script 120 is executed on that creature, to inform them that they've been selected.

commands.name: FLTO
commands.description: Move the top left corner of target to either the given screen coordinates, or the given coordinates relative to the agent it is @#FREL@ to.  Useful for floating agents.

commands.name: VOCB
commands.description: Learn all vocabulary instantly.

commands.name: CLIK
commands.description: Sets a chain of three message ids to cycle through as the agent is clicked on.  Entries of -1 are ignored.  Overriden by @#CLAC@.

commands.name: MOUS
commands.description:
Defines the behaviour of the mouse button for the default pointer behaviour - see @#PURE@.
0 is normal
1 means the right button does what the left button does
2 means the left button does what the right button does

commands.name: SPNL
commands.description: This sets the input of the neuron in the lobe specified to be the value given.

commands.name: HAIR
commands.description: Tidies or ruffles hair.  Positive means tidy, negative untidy.  There can be multiple stages of tidiness or untidiness; the more extreme the value the tidier or untidier.

commands.name: TRAN
commands.description: Sets pixel transparency awareness.  1 for pixel perfect, so transparent parts of the agent can't be clicked.  0 to allow anywhere on the agent rectangle to be clicked.  See also the option parameter on @#PAT: BUTT@ which overrides this.

commands.name: VOLM

parameters.name: volume
parameters.description: Volume in centibels (0 = full, negative = quieter, -10000 ~ silence)

commands.description: Docking Station: set the volume of an audio channel (0 = sound effects, 2 = music). Also usable as an integer RV, 'VOLM channel', to read a channel's current volume. (Creatures 3 took a single 'volume' argument.)

commands.name: SAVE
commands.description: Saves the current world at the start of the next tick.  See also @#QUIT@ for important information about using @#INST@.

commands.name: LOAD
commands.description: Loads the specified world at the start of the next tick.  See also @#QUIT@ for important information about using @#INST@.

commands.name: PURE
commands.description: Enables or disables the default clicking and moving behaviour of the pointer.  This default behaviour is to implement @#CLAC@ and @#CLIK@, and to operate ports.  Set to 1 to enable, 0 to disable.  When disabled, use @#IMSK@ to hook mouse events.

commands.name: DELW
commands.description: Deletes the specified world directory.

commands.name: PAUS
commands.description: Stops the target agent from running - it'll freeze completely, scripts and physics.  Set to 1 to pause, 0 to run.  You might want to use @#WPAU@ with this to implement a pause game option.

commands.name: STPT
commands.description: Stops any currently running script in the target agent.  See also @#STOP@.

commands.name: QUIT
commands.description: Quits the engine at the start of the next tick, without saving any changes.  Call @#SAVE@ first to make it save the current world.  If doing a sequence like \"SAVE QUIT\" or \"SAVE LOAD menu\", do it in an @#INST@ section.  Otherwise it will sometimes save between the two instructions, meaning it quits (or loads menu) immediately upon reloading.

commands.name: SCAM
commands.description: Sets the current camera to be used in subsequent camera macro commands.  This uses the given @#TARG@ and the given @#PART@ number.  If you set this to @#NULL@ then the Main Camera will be used.  This is the default setting

commands.name: ANMS
commands.description: This is like @#ANIM@, only it reads the poses from a string such as \"3 4 5 255\".  Use this when you need to dynamically construct animations.  Use ANIM in general as it is quicker to execute, although they are the same speed once the animation is underway.

commands.name: ZOOM
commands.description: Zoom in on the specified position by a negative amount of pixels or out by positive amount of pixels.  If you send -1 as the x and y coordinates then the camera zooms in on the exising view port centre.  This only applies to remote cameras.

commands.name: LINK
commands.description: Sets the permiability of the link between the rooms specified, creating the link if none exists before.  Set to 0 to close (destroy) the link.  This is used for CAs.  See also @#DOOR@.

commands.name: FRAT
commands.description: This command sets the frame rate on the @#TARG@ agent. If it is a compound agent, then the part affected can be set with the @#PART@ command. Valid rates are from 1 to 255. 1 is Normal rate, 2 is half speed etc...

commands.name: WRLD
commands.description: Creates a new world directory for the specified world.

commands.name: FCUS
commands.description: Set keyboard focus to the current @#PART@ of the targetted agent.  The part should be a @#PAT: TEXT@.  If you TARG NULL first, then no part will have the focus.

commands.name: WPAU
commands.description: Stops world ticks from running.  Days, seasons and years won't change and any delayed messages are paused, as are CAs and some sound effects.  Set to 1 to pause, 0 to run.  Use along with @#PAUS@.

commands.name: FREL
commands.description: Sets an agent for target to float relative to.  To make target actually float, you need to set attribute @#Floatable@ as well.  Set @#FREL@ to @#NULL@ to make the target float relative to the main camera - this is the default.  Use @#FLTO@ to set the relative position of the top left corner of the floating agent to the top left corner of the agent it is floating relative to.

commands.name: GRPL
commands.syntax: GRPL red green blue min_y max_y
commands.description: Add a line to a graph (previously created with @#PAT: GRPH@). The first line you add will be line 0.
commands.example: GRPL red green blue min_y max_y

commands.name: GRPV
commands.description: Add a value to a line on a graph. after you have added a value to each line on the graph, it will be updated by scrolling the current values to the left

commands.name: PSWD
commands.description: Sets the password of the current world.

commands.name: SHOW
commands.description: Set the parameter to 0 to hide the agent and to 1 to show the agent on camera.  This removes or adds the agent to the main camera and any remote cameras.  A non-shown agent can still be visible to creatures, and can still be clicked on or picked up.  It just doesn't appear on the cameras.

commands.name: FRMT
commands.syntax: FRMT left_margin top_margin right_margin bottom_margin line_spacing character_spacing justification
commands.description: Use this command to alter the appearance of the current text part. The line and character spacing values are expressed in number of extra pixels to insert between characters. Values for justification are 0 - Left, 1 - Right, 2 - Center, 4 - Bottom, 8 - Middle (you may add mutually compatible numbers).  The default format values are 8 8 8 8 0 0 0.
commands.example: FRMT left_margin top_margin right_margin bottom_margin line_spacing character_spacing justification

commands.name: SNAP
commands.syntax: SNAP filename x_centre y_centre width height zoom_factor
commands.description: This takes a photograph of the world at a particular place. The zoom parameter should be <= 100. 100 means at original size, 50 means half size etc.  It makes a new image file in the world images directory - you can use it to make agents and parts as with any image file.  Call @#SNAX@ first to check your filename isn't already in use in any images directory.  When you have finished with the file, call @#LOFT@.
commands.example: SNAP filename x_centre y_centre width height zoom_factor

commands.name: BORN
commands.description: Signals the target creature as having been born - this sends a birth event, and sets the @#TAGE@ ticking.

commands.name: NOHH
commands.description: Tell the creature to immediately stop holding hands with the pointer.  Useful when you are about to teleport a norn, it prevents the pointer from continuosly changing his position back to where it was.

commands.name: VOIS
commands.description: Sets the @#TARG@ agent's voice to the specified value. The voice name must be valid in the catalogue. If it fails, then \"DefaultVoice\" will be reloaded.  Use @#SEZZ@ to actually say something.

commands.name: VOIC
commands.description: This sets the @#TARG@ agent's voice to the specified creature voice, using standard cascade techniques to select the nearest match.  On failure, \"DefaultVoice\" will be reloaded.  Use @#SEZZ@ to actually say something.

commands.name: DEAD
commands.description: Makes the target creature die, triggering @#Die@ script and history events, closing its eyes, and stopping brain and biochemistry updates.  Not to be confused with @#KILL@, which you will have to use later to remove the actual body.

commands.name: SEZZ
commands.description: Makes the @#TARG@ agent speak the specified text with voice as set by @#VOIS@ or @#VOIC@. If @#TARG@ is a creature then it will be spoken properly (speech bubble et al).

commands.name: WTNT
commands.syntax: WTNT index red_tint green_tint blue_tint rotation swap
commands.description: This sets up the world (global) tint table. The index is the number associated with the tint table - (keep it small please) and the r,g,b is the tint level. Rotation and Swap work as for pigment bleed genes.
commands.example: WTNT index red_tint green_tint blue_tint rotation swap

commands.name: TNTW
commands.description: This tints the @#TARG@ agent with the global tint manager at index.  Specify the @#PART@ first for compound agents.  See also @#TINT@.

commands.name: TINT
commands.syntax: TINT red_tint green_tint blue_tint rotation swap
commands.description: This tints the @#TARG@ agent with the r,g,b tint and applies the colour rotation and swap as per pigment bleed genes.  Specify the @#PART@ first for compound agents.  The tinted agent or part now uses a cloned gallery, which means it takes up more memory, and the save world files are larger.  However it also no longer needs the sprite file.  Also, tinting resets camera shy and other properties of the gallery.
commands.example: TINT red_tint green_tint blue_tint rotation swap

commands.name: TINO
commands.syntax: TINO red green blue rotation swap
commands.description: Works like @#TINT@, but only applies the tint to the current frame and discards the rest.  NOTE: in this rebuild TINO currently applies the tint like TINT (whole gallery) - the current-frame-only behaviour needs a per-frame recolour and is a TODO.
commands.example: TINO red green blue rotation swap

commands.name: RGAM
commands.description: Refresh all settings that are always read from game variables at start up e.g. the length of a day.  This allows you to change such setting on the fly.

commands.name: REAF
commands.description: Refreshes the catalogue from files on disk, from the main catalogue directory and the world catalogue directory.  These are normally read in at startup, when a new world is read in, or when the PRAY resources system installs a catalogue file.  Use while developing CAOS programs to refresh the catalogue as you add entries.

commands.name: NEWC
commands.syntax: NEWC family gene_agent gene_slot sex variant
commands.description: This version of @#NEW: CREA@ executes over a series of ticks, helping to prevent the pause caused by the creation of a creature with the @#NEW: CREA@ command. However, it cannot be used in install scripts (e.g. the bootstrap) and so @#NEW: CREA@ should be used for that.
commands.example: NEWC family gene_agent gene_slot sex variant

commands.name: FRSH
commands.description: Refreshes the main view port.

commands.name: BRMI
commands.description: Sets the Map's Metaroom and Room index bases for adding new rooms/metarooms.

commands.name: CABW
commands.description: Set the capacity or width of the cabin.  This will determine how many passengers the cabin can hold, each passenger will be on a separate plane within the cabin.  Use @#CABP@ to set the plane of the first agent relative to the cabin.  The default width is zero, this means that the cabin will accept any number of passengers and will place them all on the same plane.

commands.name: DOCA
commands.description: Updates all CAs the specified number of times.

commands.name: PAGE
commands.description: Sets current page for text part. The page number should be equal or greater than zero and less than the number returned by @#NPGS@. Use @#PAT: TEXT@ or @#PAT: FIXD@ to make a text part, and @#PART@ to set the current part.

commands.name: DONE
commands.description: Stops the targetted creature doing any involuntary actions.

commands.name: STRK
commands.description: This triggers the music track specified. The track will play for at least latency seconds before being overridden by room or metaroom music.

commands.name: WDOW
commands.description: Toggle full screen mode.

commands.name: FORF
commands.description: Set the friends or foe lobe to learn from the creature.

commands.name: LIKE
commands.description: State a personal opinion about a creature.

commands.name: MIRA
commands.description: Tell the agent to draw the current sprite mirrored (send 1 as a parameter) or normally (send 0 as a parameter)

commands.name: ZOMB
commands.description: Make or undo the creature's zombification factor.  1 makes creatures zombies: in a zombie state creatures won't process any decision scripts but they will respond to @ANIM@s and @POSE@s.  0 umzombifies.

commands.name: CABV
commands.description: Sets the room number which things in the cabin think they are in.  By default, the value is -1, and the room is the one underneath wherever the agent happens to be.  Make sure you set this if the vehicle ever remotely leaves the room system.  This command effects values returned from @#ROOM@ and @#GRID@.  It won't apply to some aspects of Creatures in the vehicle.

commands.name: HAND
commands.description: Sets the name of the hand. Bt default this is 'hand'.

commands.name: MANN
commands.description: Outputs help on the given command to the output stream.

commands.name: HELP
commands.description: Lists all command names to the output stream.

commands.name: APRO
commands.description: Lists all command names whose help contains the text.

commands.name: MEMX
commands.description: Sends information about the memory allocated to the output stream.  In order, these are the Memory Load (unknown), Total Physical (size in bytes of physical memory), Available Physical (free physical space), Total Page File (maximum possible size of page file), Available Page File (size in bytes of space available in paging file), Total Virtual (size of user mode portion of the virtual address space of the engine), Available Virtual (size of unreserved and uncommitted memory in the user mode portion of the virtual address space of the engine).

commands.name: SIMP
commands.syntax: SIMP family genus species sprite_file image_count first_image plane
commands.description: Create a new simple agent, using the specified sprite file. The agent will have image_count sprites available, starting at first_image in the file. The plane is the screen depth to show the agent at - the higher the number, the nearer the camera.
commands.example: SIMP family genus species sprite_file image_count first_image plane

commands.name: COMP
commands.syntax: COMP family genus species sprite_file image_count first_image plane
commands.description: Create a new compound agent. The sprite file is for the first part, which is made automatically.  Similarly, image_count and first_image are for that first part.  The plane is the absolute plane of part 1 - the planes of other parts are relative to the first part.
commands.example: COMP family genus species sprite_file image_count first_image plane

commands.name: VHCL
commands.syntax: VHCL family genus species sprite_file image_count first_image plane
commands.description: Create a new vehicle.  Parameters are the same as @#NEW: COMP@.
commands.example: VHCL family genus species sprite_file image_count first_image plane

commands.name: WRIT
commands.description: Send a message to another agent.  The message_id is from the table of @#Message Numbers@; remember that early @#Message Numbers@ differ slightly from @#Script Numbers@.  If used from an install script, then @#FROM@ for the message to @#NULL@ rather than @#OWNR@.

commands.name: SHOU
commands.description: Shout a stimulus to all creatures who can hear @#OWNR@.  The strength is a multiplier for the stimulus.  Set to 1 for a default stimulation, 2 for a stronger stimulation and so on.  It is important you use this, rather than send several stims, as it affects learning.  Set strength to 0 to prevent learning altogether, and send a strength 1 chemical change.  See the table of @#Stimulus Numbers@.

commands.name: SIGN
commands.description: Send a stimulus to all creatures who can see @#OWNR@.

commands.name: TACT
commands.description: Send a stimulus to all creatures who are touching @#OWNR@.

commands.name: ROOT
commands.description: Output the family numbers for which there are scripts in the scriptorium.  List is space delimited.

commands.name: INEW
commands.syntax: INEW id name description x y message_num
commands.description: Create a new input port on target. You should number input port ids starting at 0.  The message_num is the message that will be sent to the agent when a signal comes in through the input port. _P1_ of that message will contain the data value of the signal. The position of the port, relative to the agent, is given by x, y.
commands.example: INEW id name description x y message_num

commands.name: IZAP
commands.description: Remove the specified input port.

commands.name: ONEW
commands.syntax: ONEW id name description x y
commands.description: Create a new output port on target. You should number input port ids starting at 0.  The port's relative position is given by x, y.
commands.example: ONEW id name description x y

commands.name: OZAP
commands.description: Remove the specified output port.

commands.name: JOIN
commands.description: Connect an output port on the source agent to an input port on the destination. An input may only be connected to one output at at time, but an output may feed any number of inputs.

commands.name: SEND
commands.description: Send a signal from the specified output port to all connected inputs.  The data can be any integer.

commands.name: BANG
commands.description: Breaks connections randomly with other machines (as if the machine had been 'banged'. Use a bang_strength of 100 to disconnect all ports, 50 to disconnect about half etc.

commands.name: KRAK
commands.description: Breaks a specific connection on a machine. If in_or_out is zero, it is an input port whose connection is broken, if it is an output port, then all inputs are disconnected.

commands.name: DULL
commands.syntax: DULL part_id sprite_file first_image rel_x rel_y rel_plane
commands.description: Create a dull part for a compound agent.  A dull part does nothing except show an image from the given sprite file.  You should number part ids starting at 1, as part 0 is automatically made when the agent is made.  The dull part's position is relative to part 0, as is its plane.  Use @#PART@ to select it before you change @#POSE@ or @#ANIM@, or use various other commands.
commands.example: DULL part_id sprite_file first_image rel_x rel_y rel_plane

commands.name: BUTT
commands.syntax: BUTT part_id sprite_file first_image image_count rel_x rel_y rel_plane anim_hover message_id option
commands.description:
Create a button on a compound agent. anim_hover is an animation, as in the @#ANIM@ command, to use when the mouse is over the button - when the mouse is moved off, it returns to any previous animation that was going. message_id is sent when the button is clicked. option is 0 for the mouse to hit anywhere in the bounding box, 1 to hit only non-transparent pixels.
@#_P1_@ of the message is set to the part number of the buttons allowing you to overload your messages by button group and then switch on input value in the script.
commands.example: BUTT part_id sprite_file first_image image_count rel_x rel_y rel_plane anim_hover message_id option

commands.name: TEXT
commands.syntax: TEXT part_id sprite_file first_image rel_x rel_y rel_plane message_id font_sprite
commands.description: Creates a text entry part.  Gains the focus when you click on it, or with the @#FCUS@ command.  Sends the message_id when tab or return are pressed - a good place to use @#PTXT@ to get the text out, and to set the focus elsewhere.
commands.example: TEXT part_id sprite_file first_image rel_x rel_y rel_plane message_id font_sprite

commands.name: FIXD
commands.syntax: FIXD part_id sprite_file first_image rel_x rel_y rel_plane font_sprite
commands.description: Create a fixed text part. The text is wrapped on top of the supplied gallery image. new-line characters may be used.  Use @#PTXT@ to set the text.
commands.example: FIXD part_id sprite_file first_image rel_x rel_y rel_plane font_sprite

commands.name: GRPH
commands.syntax: GRPH part_id overlay_sprite baseimage relx rely relplane numValues
commands.description: Creates a graph part on a compound agent. Use @#GRPL@ to add a line to the graph and @#GRPV@ to add a value to a graph line.
commands.example: GRPH part_id overlay_sprite baseimage relx rely relplane numValues

commands.name: SETN
commands.description: Sets a neuron weight.

commands.name: SETD
commands.description: Sets a dendrite weight.

commands.name: SETL
commands.description: Sets a lobe's SV rule float value.

commands.name: SETT
commands.description: Sets a tract's SV rule float value.

commands.name: DMPB
commands.description: Dumps the sizes of the binary data dumps for current lobes and tracts.

commands.name: DMPL
commands.description: Dumps a lobe as binary data.

commands.name: DMPT
commands.description: Dumps a tract as binary data.

commands.name: DMPN
commands.description: Dumps a neuron as binary data.

commands.name: DMPD
commands.description: Dumps a dendrite as binary data.

commands.name: PLAY
commands.description: This command undoes a previously given @#DBG: PAWS@ and allows game time to flow as normal.

commands.name: TOCK
commands.description: This command forces a tick to occur. It is useful in external apps to drive the game according to a different clock instead of the game clock.

commands.name: FLSH
commands.description: This flushes the system's input buffers - usually only useful if @#DBG: PAWS@ed.

commands.name: POLL
commands.description: This takes all of the @#DBG: OUTV@ and @#DBG: OUTS@ output to date and writes it to the output stream.

commands.name: PROF
commands.description: Sends agent profile information to the output stream.  This gives you data about the time the engine spends running the update and message handling code for each classifier.  The data is measured from engine startup, or the point marked with @#DBG: CPRO@.  It's output in comma separated value (CSV) format, so you can load it into a spreadsheet for sorting and summing.

commands.name: CPRO
commands.description: Clears agent profiling information.  Measurements output with @#DBG: PROF@ start here.

commands.name: HTML
commands.description: Sends CAOS documentation to the output stream.  Sort order is 0 for alphabetical, 1 for categorical.

commands.name: ASRT
commands.description: Confirms that a condition is true.  If it isn't, it displays a runtime error dialog.

commands.name: REFR
commands.description: This command refreshes the engine's view of the Resource directory. Execute this if you have reason to believe that the files in the directory may have changed. This forces a @#PRAY GARB@ to happen automatically

commands.name: GARB
commands.description: This command clears the manager's cached resource data. Execute this after a lot of resource accesses (E.g. installing an agent) to clean up the memory used during the process. If you don't do this, excess memory can be held for a while, If the parameter is zero (the most usual) then the manager will only forget resources which are not in use at the moment. If force is non-zero, then the manager will forget all the previously loaded resources. As the resources currently in use go out of scope, they are automatically garbage collected.

commands.name: CROS
commands.syntax: CROS child_agent child_slot mum_agent mum_slot dad_agent dad_slot mum_chance_of_mutation mum_degree_of_mutation dad_chance_of_mutation dad_degree_of_mutation.
commands.description: Crosses two genomes with mutation, and fills in a child geneme slot.  Mutation variables may be in the range of 0 to 255.
commands.example: CROS child_agent child_slot mum_agent mum_slot dad_agent dad_slot mum_chance_of_mutation mum_degree_of_mutation dad_chance_of_mutation dad_degree_of_mutation.

commands.name: MOVE
commands.description: Moves a genome from one slot to another.

commands.name: CLON
commands.description: Clones a genome, creating a new moniker and copying the genetics file.

commands.name: OOPE
commands.description:
Sets the file for the output stream of the current virtual machine - there is a virtual machine for each agent, so this is much the same as setting it for @#OWNR@. Use @#OUTV@ and @#OUTS@ or various other commands to send text data to the stream. The filename should include any file extension.

You should use @#FILE OCLO@ to close the file, although this happens automatically if you set a new file, if the virtual machine is destroyed, or if the engine exits.

Directory is 0 for the current world's journal directory, or 1 for the main journal directory. Set append to 1 to add to the end of the file, or 0 to replace any existing file.

commands.name: OCLO
commands.description: Disconnects anything which is attached to the output stream.  If this is a file, then the file is closed.

commands.name: OFLU
commands.description: Flush output stream.  If it is attached to a disk file, this will force any data in the buffer to be written to disk.

commands.name: IOPE
commands.description:
Sets the file for the input stream of the current virtual machine - there is a virtual machine for each agent, so this is much the same as setting it for @#OWNR@. Use @#INNL@, @#INNI@ and @#INNF@ to get data from the stream, and @#INOK@ to check validity of the stream. The filename should include any file extension.

You should use @#FILE ICLO@ to close the file, although this happens automatically if you set a new file, if the virtual machine is destroyed, or if the engine exits.

Directory is 0 for the current world's journal directory, or 1 for the main journal directory.

commands.name: ICLO
commands.description: Disconnects anything which is attached to the input stream.  If this is a file, then the file is closed.

commands.name: JDEL
commands.description: This deletes the file (filename) specified from the journal directory specified. If directory is zero, this is the current world's journal directory, otherwise it is the main journal directory.  It deletes the file immediately, rather than marking it for the attic.

commands.name: EVNT
commands.description: Triggers a life event of the given type.  Some events are triggered automatically by the engine, some events need triggering from CAOS, others are custom events that you can use for your own purposes.  See @#HIST TYPE@ for details of the event numbers.  All new events made call the @#Life Event@ script.

commands.name: UTXT
commands.description: For the given life event, sets the user text.

commands.name: NAME

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Variable key - anything at all: an integer, float, string or agent

commands.description: A named variable stored on the target (TARG) agent, addressed by an arbitrary key instead of a numeric index - effectively a named OVxx variable. The key and the value may each be an integer, float, string or agent. Reading a key that has never been set returns the integer 0 (the variable is created on first write). Use @#NAMN@ to enumerate the NAME variables present on an agent. NOTE: in this web rebuild NAME variables are not yet saved with the world - see DOCUMENTATION/DS/name_variables.md. See also @#NAMN@, @#MAME@, @#GAME@ and the OVxx variables.

commands.name: MAME

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Variable key - anything at all: an integer, float, string or agent

commands.description: A named variable stored on the OWNR agent, addressed by an arbitrary key - the OWNR-scoped sibling of @#NAME@ (exactly as MVxx is to OVxx). The key and the value may each be an integer, float, string or agent. Reading a key that has never been set returns the integer 0 (created on first write). NOTE: in this web rebuild MAME variables are not yet saved with the world - see DOCUMENTATION/DS/name_variables.md. See also @#NAME@, @#GAME@ and the MVxx variables.

commands.name: UPPA

parameters.name: string
parameters.description: String to convert to upper case

commands.description: Returns the given string converted to upper case.  Characters which are not lower-case letters are unaffected.  The sibling of @#LOWA@.

commands.name: WIPE
commands.description: Purge the creature history for the given moniker.  Only applies if the genome isn't referenced by any slot, and the creature is fully dead or exported.  Use @#OOWW@ to test this first.

commands.name: FOTO
commands.description:
For the given life event, sets the associated photograph. Use @#SNAP@ to take the photograph first.

If there was already a photograph for the event, then it is automatically marked for the attic as in @#LOFT@, and overwritten with the new photo. Hence you can use an empty string to clear a photo. If @#HIST WIPE@ is used to clear the event, the photo is similarly stored in the attic.

It is considered an error to send a photograph that is in use (unless cloned with @#TINT@) to the attic. If this happens, you will get a runtime error. You should either be confident that no agents are using the photo, or call @#LOFT@ first to test if they are.

commands.name: DOIF
commands.description:
Execute a block of code if the condition is true. The code block ends at the next @#ELSE@, @#ELIF@ or @#ENDI@. A condition is composed of one or more comparisons joined by AND or OR. A comparison compares two values with EQ, NE, GT, GE, LT, LE, or alternatively =, <>, >, >=, <, <=.

DOIF ov00 GE 5 AND ov00 LT 10
--- code block 1 ---
ELIF ov00 GE 10 OR ov00 LT 100
--- code block 2 ---
ELSE
--- code block 3 ---
ENDI

Conditions are evaluated simply from left to right, so "a AND b OR c" is the same as "(a AND b) OR c", not "a AND ( b OR c )".

Conditional statements may not work correctly with commands overloaded by rvalue.

commands.name: ELIF
commands.description: ELseIF command to follow a @#DOIF@. If the condition in a DOIF is false, each following ELIF command will be evaluated in turn.  Only the first true condition will have its code block executed.

commands.name: ELSE
commands.description: ELSE clause to follow @#DOIF@ and @#ELIF@(s). If nothing else matches, the ELSE block will be executed.

commands.name: ENDI
commands.description: Closes a @#DOIF@...@#ELIF@...@#ELSE@... set.

commands.name: ENUM
commands.description: Iterate through each agent which conforms to the given classification, setting @#TARG@ to point to each valid agent in turn. family, genus and/or species can be zero to act as wildcards.  @#NEXT@ terminates the block of code which is executed with each TARG.  After an ENUM, TARG is set to @#OWNR@.

commands.name: ESEE
commands.description: As @#ENUM@, except only enumerates through agents which @#OWNR@ can see.  An agent can see another if it is within @#RNGE@, its @#PERM@ allows it to see through all intervening walls, and for creatures @#ATTR@ @#Invisible@ isn't set.  See also @#STAR@ and @#SEEE@.  In install scripts, when there is no @#OWNR@, @#TARG@ is used instead.

commands.name: ETCH
commands.description: As @#ENUM@, except only enumerates through agents which @#OWNR@ is touching.  Agents are said to be touching if their bounding rectangles overlap.  See also @#TTAR@.  In install scripts, when there is no @#OWNR@, @#TARG@ is used instead.

commands.name: EPAS
commands.description: Enumerate over owner vehicle's passengers which match the given classifier.  Similar to @#ENUM@.

commands.name: NEXT
commands.description: Closes an enumeration loop.  The loop can begin with @#ENUM@, @#ESEE@, @#ETCH@ or @#EPAS@.

commands.name: REPS
commands.description: Loop through a block of code a number of times. Must have a matching @#REPE@ command to close the block.

commands.name: REPE
commands.description: Closes a @#REPS@ loop.

commands.name: LOOP
commands.description: Begin a LOOP..@#UNTL@ or LOOP..@#EVER@ loop.

commands.name: UNTL
commands.description: Forms the end of a @#LOOP@..UNTL loop. The loop will execute until the condition is met.  See @#DOIF@ for information on the form of the condition.

commands.name: EVER
commands.description: Forms the end of a @#LOOP@..EVER loop, which just loops forever.

commands.name: SUBR
commands.description: Defines the start of a subroutine. Specify a label after the @#SUBR@ command - the label is case sensitive, and should start with a letter. If this instruction is hit during normal program flow, it works as a @#STOP@ instruction.  See @#GSUB@ and @#RETN@.

commands.name: ECON
commands.description: Starts an enumeration across all the agents in a connective system, where agent is any agent within the connective system.

commands.name: DELN
commands.description: Deletes the specified @#NAME@ variable on @#TARG@.

commands.name: DELE
commands.description: Deletes the specified @#EAME@ variable.

commands.name: ALPH
commands.description: The agent will be drawn alpha blended against the background by the given value - from 256 for invisible to 0 for completely solid.  For compound agents set the @#PART@ to affect a particular part or to -1 to affect all parts.  The second parameter switches alpha blending on (1) or off (0).  Alpha graphics are drawn much slower, so use sparingly and turn it off completely rather than using an intensity value of 0 or 256.  At the moment alpha channels only work on compressed, non-mirrored, non-zoomed sprites.

commands.name: PLMD
commands.description: Dumps out all the dendrite learned information of the specified tract to a file (will be changed to sync with Palm).

commands.name: PLMU
commands.description: Configures the dendrites in the specified tract with the data in the file (will be changed to sync with Palm).

commands.name: NOTV
commands.description: Peform a bitwise NOT on an integer variable.

commands.name: BUZZ
commands.description: Sets the ideal interval in milliseconds between each tick.  However fast the machine, it won't tick quicker than this, but it might tick slower.  You can find the actual time taken with @#RACE@.  Changing this from the default value of 50 midgame will damage profiling and seasons.  Things such as creature brains are designed for the default 50 millisecond update interval.  Change this with caution!

commands.name: CALG
commands.description: Choose how a creature (TARG) decides which particular object in a category to look at.  PICK_NEAREST_IN_X_DIRECTION=0, PICK_A_RANDOM_ONE=1, PICK_NEAREST_IN_CURRENT_ROOM=2, PICK_NEAREST_TO_GROUND=3, PICK_RANDOM_NEAREST_IN_X_DIRECTION=4.

commands.name: NAMN
commands.description: Enumerates through @#NAME@ variable names, roughly as @#GAMN@ does through @#GAME@ variables.  Start and end with an empty string.

commands.name: VARC
commands.description: [not implemented yet]

commands.name: DOIN
commands.description: Make the creature TARG process N instincts.

commands.name: ADIN
commands.description: Add an instinct to the creature's brain queue.  (The instinct is not processed immediately).  Example:  ADIN 3 4 0.5 7 encourages (by a factor of 0.5) the creature to do action 3 on category 4 when drive 7 is high.

commands.name: BOOT
commands.description: Loads in a list of numbered bootstrap folders contained within a folder called subboot. Bootstraps folders numbers are powers of 2, sum the folder numbers to load those folders.  There is provision for more than one subboot folder, these should be uniquely numbered.

commands.name: WEBB
commands.description: Launches an external URL in the user's browser. The game engine adds http:// at the beginning to prevent malicious launching of programs, so you just need to specify the domain name and path.

commands.name: CATO
commands.description: Change the target's category to the one specified.  The default is -1 which means the category is based on classifier and the catalogue as described in @#CATI@.  See also @#CATX@ and @#CATA@.

commands.name: CALC
commands.description: Recalculates all the navigational CAs (warning: slow).

commands.name: UCLN
commands.description: Make sure that an agent isn't cloned anymore, this releases the memory taken up by @#TINT@ing it. Agents are usually cloned for purposes such as tinting. Don't forget to set the relevant @#PART@ number for compound agents.

commands.name: MIND
commands.description: Enable (1) or disable (0) the creature's brain (unlike @#ZOMB#@ in that the brain actually stops processing and it's output is frozen onto the one noun and verb).

commands.name: CORE
commands.description: Sets the bounding box of the physical core of the object TARG.  May be set to smaller (or larger) than the sprite's rectangle.

commands.name: DCOR
commands.description: Debug command to show the physical core of the TARG agent graphically.

commands.name: MOTR
commands.description: Enable (1) or disable (0) the creature's motor faculty, i.e. whether it sets the IT object and fires off scripts.

commands.name: DSEE
commands.description: Debug command to show all the agents which can be seen by any creature.

commands.name: SOUL
commands.description: Enable (1) or disable (0) the update on the creature's faculty as given by type id as follows: Sensory Faculty (0), Brain (1), Motor Faculty (2), Linguistic Faculty (3), Biochemistry (4), Reproductive Faculty (5), Expressive Faculty (6), Music Faculty (7), Life Faculty (8)

commands.name: STEP
commands.description: Does one update of the specified faculty (for faculty id see @#SOUL#@).

commands.name: JECT
commands.description:
Injects a COS file from the bootstrap directory. The file is searched for (case insensitively) in all bootstrap subdirectories. You must specify the file extension (it doesn't have to be .cos). Flags is a combination of what you want to inject:

1 - Remove sctipt
2 - Event scripts
4 - Install script

The scripts (if present) are injected in that order. So, setting flags to 7 will fully uninstall and reinstall the cos file. Error messages and output are written to the current output stream.

commands.name: CREA
commands.syntax: NEW: CREA family gene_agent gene_slot sex variant
commands.description: Makes a creature using the genome from the given gene slot in another agent.  You'll want to use @#GENE CROS@ or @#GENE LOAD@ to fill that slot in first.  The gene slot is cleared, as control of that genome is moved to the special slot 0 of the new creature, where it is expressed.  Sex is 1 for male, 2 for female or 0 for random.  The variant can also be 0 for a random value between 1 and 8.  See also @#NEWC@.

commands.name: CRAG
commands.syntax: NEW: CRAG family gene_agent gene_slot sex variant sprite_file image_count first_image plane
commands.description: Makes a non-skeletal creature.  The first five arguments are the same as @#NEW: CREA@.  The last four, starting from the sprite file, are exactly as in @#NEW: COMP@.

commands.name: WRT+
commands.syntax: MESG WRT+ agent message_id param_1 param_2 delay
commands.description: Send a message with parameters to another agent.  Waits delay ticks before sending the message.  The message_id is from the table of @#Message Numbers@.

commands.name: FMLY
commands.description: Output the genus numbers for which there are scripts in the scriptorium for the given family.  List is space delimited.

commands.name: GNUS
commands.description: Output the species numbers for which there are scripts in the scriptorium for the given family and genus.  List is space delimited.

commands.name: SPCS
commands.description: Output the event numbers of scripts in the scriptorium for the given classifier.  List is space delimited.

commands.name: PAWS
commands.description: This pauses everything in the game. No game driven ticks will occur until a @#DBG: PLAY@ command is issued, so this command is only useful for debugging.  Use @#PAUS@ for pausing of specific agents, which you can use to implement a pause button.

commands.name: WTIK
commands.description: Changes the world tick @#WTIK@ to the given value.  This should only be used for debugging, as it will potentially leave confusing information in the creature history, and change the time when delayed messages are processed.  Its main use is to jump to different seasons and times of day.

commands.name: TACK
commands.description: Pauses the game when the given agent next executes a single line of CAOS code.  This pause is mid-tick, and awaits incoming requests, or the pause key.  Either another DBG: TACK or a @#DBG: PLAY@ command will make the engine carry on.  Any other incoming requests will be processed as normal.  However, the virtual machine of the tacking agent is effectively in mid-processing, so some CAOS commands may cause unpredictable results, and even crash the engine.  In particular, you shouldn't @#KILL@ the tacking agent.  You can see which agent is being tracked with @#TACK@.

commands.name: COUN
commands.description: This returns the number of resource chunks which are tagged with the resource type passed in. Resource types are four characters only. Anything over that length will be silently truncated.

commands.name: AGTI
commands.description: This returns the value of the integer tag associated with the named resource. If the resource does not contain such a tag, then the default value specified is returned. This call pairs with @#PRAY AGTS@.

commands.name: DEPS
commands.description:
This performs a scan of the specified resource, and checks out the dependency data. The primary use for this would be in the preparation for injection of agents. If you pass zero in the do_install parameter, then the dependencies are only checked. If do_install is non-zero, then they are installed also. The return values are as follows:
0 = Success
-1 = Agent Type not found
-2 = Dependency Count not found
-3 to -(2 + count) is the dependency string missing
-(3+count) to -(2+2*count) is the dependency type missing
2*count to 3*count is the category ID for that dependency being invalid
1 to count is the dependency failing

commands.name: FILE
commands.description: This performs the "installation" of one file from the resource files. The resource_type is defined in the agent resource guide. If do_install is zero, the command simply checks if the file install should succeed. Return value is 0 for success, 1 for error.

commands.name: TEST
commands.description:
This checks for the existence of a chunk, returning zero if it is not found, and a value from 1-3 indicating the cost to load if it is.
Return values are currently defined as:
0 - Chunk not available at this time
1 - Chunk Available, Cached and ready for use
2 - Chunk available, on disk uncompressed and fine for loading
3 - Chunk available, on disk compressed and ready for loading.

Thus the return value could be thought of as the cost of loading, where 1 is no cost, and 3 is high cost.

commands.name: INJT
commands.description:
This command injects an agent. The agent must be in the chunk named. If do_install is zero, the command simply checks for the presence of the required scripts and dependencies. If non-zero, it attempts to inject the agent. The report var is a string variable, and is set to the name of the offending script if the injection/check fails.
Return is 0 for success, -1 for "Script not found" and if injecting, -2 for "Injection failed".
Return value -3 indicates that a dependency evaluation failed, and in this case, the report var is the return code from @#PRAY DEPS@

commands.name: EXPO
commands.description:
This function exports the target creature. If the creature is exported successfully then it has been removed from the world. Returns value is one of the following:
0 for success
1 if the creature, or if pregnant any of its offspring, are already on disk in some form.

The chunk type should be used to find the creature again to import it. In Creatures 3, most exported creatures have a chunk type EXPC, and the starter family uses SFAM.

For new games, you should not use SFAM, as its data would get confused with that of an EXPC with the same moniker. This is for backwards compatibility with Creatures 3's use of SFAM, which works because the CAOS code guarantees different monikers.

For other chunk names, creatures exported with a different type are kept entirely separately, and will not get confused with each other. The chunk type is added to the end of the moniker to form the chunk name.

The exported creature has some fields associated with it, that can be read by @#PRAY AGTI@ or @#PRAY AGTS@ before importing:
"Exported At World Time" integer
"Creature Age In Ticks" integer
"Exported At Real Time" integer
"Creature Life Stage" integer
"Exported From World Name" string
"Exported From World UID" string
"Native Network User" string
"Last Network User" (could be faked, @#NET: FROM@ is safer) string
"Creature Name" string
"Gender" integer
"Genus" integer
"Variant" integer
"Head Gallery" string (this is calculated on the sending computer, so the file may be missing on the receiving one - try @#LIMB@ instead)
"Pregnancy Status" integer

In addition you can add custom fields by setting @#NAME@ variables on the Creature before export. Any strings or integers whose name begin "Pray Extra " are added as entries to the export file.

commands.name: IMPO
commands.description:
This function imports the creature with the requested moniker and chunk type. Returns one of the following codes:
0 - success
1 - couldn't reconcile histories so creature was cloned
2 - moniker not found in PRAY system
3 - unused error code
4 - internal / file format error

Set actually_do_it to 1 to try and perform the import, or 0 to perform a query giving just the return value. You can use the query to test if the creature is available, and if the creature would have to be cloned upon importing, and warn the user. The new creature is @#TARG@etted after import. If you set keep file to 1, then the exported file won't be deleted (moved to the porch). The creature will appear in the same place that it was exported, but as with @#NEW: CREA@, it will be in limbo, and won't function until moved to a valid place.

commands.name: MAKE
commands.syntax: PRAY MAKE which_journal_spot journal_name which_pray_spot pray_name report_destination
commands.description:
Please see the documentation accompanying the praybuilder on CDN

Suffice it to say: return value is zero for success, otherwise non-zero, and report is set to the praybuilder output for you

Also, the which_journal_spot is zero for world journal, 1 for global journal. Also the which_pray_spot is zero for "My Agents" and 1 for "My Creatures"

commands.name: PREV
commands.description: This returns the name of the resource chunk directly before the named one, given that they are of the same type. It loops when it reaches the end.  If the named resource cannot be found in the list of resources of the type specified, then the first resource of that type is returned. This call pairs with @#PRAY NEXT@.  Compare @#PRAY BACK@.

commands.name: AGTS
commands.description: This returns the value of the string tag associated with the named resource. If the resource does not contain such a tag, then the default value specified is returned. This call pairs with @#PRAY AGTI@.

commands.name: BACK
commands.description: Like @#PRAY PREV@, only doesn't loop at the end.  If you go beyond the first entry then it returns an empty string.

commands.name: FORE
commands.description: Like @#PRAY NEXT@, only doesn't loop at the end.  If you go beyond the last entry then it returns an empty string.

commands.name: GLOB
commands.description:
This globs a journal directory (0 for world one, 1 for main one) for the filespec provided. As all this can do is list files, it does not worry about where you look relative to the journal directory in question. Use this with care.

Having globbed a directory, the listing is available on the input stream as a number, followed by the names of each file. To read - ise @#INOK@, @#INNI@ and @#INNL@. Once you have finished, remember to do a @#FILE ICLO@ to remove the glob output from the VM.

commands.name: TYPE
commands.description:
For the given life event, returns its type.

All histories begin with one of the following four events. You can read the associated monikers with @#HIST MON1@ and @#HIST MON2@.
0 Conceived - a natural start to life, associated monikers are the mother's and father's
1 Spliced - created using @#GENE CROS@ to crossover the two associated monikers
2 Engineered - from a human made genome with @#GENE LOAD@, the first associated moniker is blank, and the second is the filename
14 Cloned - such as when importing a creature that already exists in the world and reallocating the new moniker, when @#TWIN@ing or @#GENE CLON@ing; associated moniker is who we were cloned from

The following events happen during a creature's life:
3 Born - triggered by the @#BORN@ command, associated monikers are the parents.
4 Aged - reached the next life stage, either naturally from the ageing loci or with @#AGES@
5 Exported - emmigrated to another world
6 Imported - immigrated back again
7 Died - triggered naturally with the death trigger locus, or by the @#DEAD@ command
8 Became pregnant - the first associated moniker is the child, and the second the father
9 Impregnated - first associated moniker is the child, second the mother
10 Child born - first moniker is the child, second the other parent
15 Clone source - someone was cloned from you, first moniker is whom
16 Warped out - exported through a worm hole with @#NET: EXPO@
17 Warped in - imported through a worm hole

These events aren't triggered by the engine, but reserved for CAOS to use with these numbers:
11 Laid by mother
12 Laid an egg
13 Photographed

Other numbers can also be used for custom life events. Start with numbers 100 and above, as events below that are reserved for the engine. You send your own events using @#HIST EVNT@.

commands.name: TAGE
commands.description: Returns the age in ticks of the creature when the given life event happened to it.  If the creature was not in the world, wasn't born yet, or was fully dead, then -1 is returned.  If the creature was dead, but its body still in the world, then its age on death is returned.  See also @#TAGE@.

commands.name: RTIM
commands.description: Returns the real world time when the given life event happened.  This is measured in seconds since midnight, 1 January 1970 in UTC.  To display, use @#RTIF@.

commands.name: CAGE
commands.description: Returns the life stage of the creature when the given life event happened.

commands.name: GEND
commands.description: Returns the sex that the creature with the given moniker has or had.  1 for male, 2 for female.  If the creature hasn't been born yet, returns -1.

commands.name: VARI
commands.description: Returns the variant that the creature with the given moniker has or had.  If the creature hasn't been born yet, returns -1.

commands.name: WVET
commands.description: Returns 1 if the Creature is a warp hole veteran, 0 otherwise.  The creature is a veteran if they have ever been exported with @#NET: EXPO@.  They must have been the main exported creature - warping as an embryo doesn't make you a veteran.

commands.name: FIND
commands.description: Searches for a life event of a certain @#HIST TYPE@ for the given moniker. The search begins at the life event after the from index. Specify -1 to find the first event. Returns the event number, or -1 if there is no matching event.

commands.name: FINR
commands.description: Reverse searches for a life event of a certain @#HIST TYPE@ for the given moniker. The search begins at the life event before the from index. Specify -1 to find the last event. Returns the event number, or -1 if there is no matching event.

commands.name: SEAN
commands.description: Returns the current season for a given world tick.  This is the same as @#SEAN@.  See also @#WTIK@ and @#HIST WTIK@.

commands.name: TIME
commands.description: Returns the time of day for a given world tick.  This is the same as @#TIME@.  See also @#WTIK@ and @#HIST WTIK@.

commands.name: YEAR
commands.description: Returns the number of game years elapsed for a given world tick.  This is the same as @#YEAR@.  See also @#WTIK@ and @#HIST WTIK@.

commands.name: DATE
commands.description: Returns the day within the current season.  This is the same as @#DATE@.  See also @#WTIK@ and @#HIST WTIK@.

commands.name: MUTE
commands.description: Returns the number of point mutations the genome received during crossover from its parents.

commands.name: MON1
commands.description: For the given life event, returns the first associated moniker.

commands.name: MON2
commands.description: For the given life event, returns the second associated moniker.

commands.name: WNAM
commands.description: Returns the name of the world the given life event happened in.

commands.name: WUID
commands.description: Returns the unique identifier of the world the given life event happened in.

commands.name: NETU
commands.description: Returns the network identifier of the user when the given life event happened.

commands.name: ITOT
